title: How the official and supplemental measures differ
description: Source-specific comparison of the units, resources, thresholds, universe and use of the two measures.
methodology: Eight definitions paraphrase the original federal statistical publication. These are methodological definitions, not eight population observations.

source.title: Poverty in the United States: 2024
source.locator: Differences in Poverty Measures, printed pp.2–3 / physical pp.8–9

values.official: People related by birth, marriage or adoption form a family; unrelated individuals are measured separately.
values.supplemental: The unit also includes unmarried partners and their relatives, coresident unrelated children under 15, and foster children under 22.

rows.note: Plain-language paraphrase tied to the specified original source location.

values.official: The historical base is three times the cost of a minimum food diet in 1963, updated for prices.
values.supplemental: Recent expenditure on food, clothing, shelter, utilities, telephone and internet.

rows.note: Plain-language paraphrase tied to the specified original source location.

values.official: Thresholds vary by family size, composition and householder age; the statistical thresholds do not vary geographically.
values.supplemental: Thresholds vary by family size, composition and housing tenure, and reflect geographic differences in housing costs.

rows.note: Plain-language paraphrase tied to the specified original source location.

values.official: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, all items.
values.supplemental: Most recent five-year moving average of the specified expenditures, lagged one year.

rows.note: Plain-language paraphrase tied to the specified original source location.

values.official: Pretax cash income; excludes tax credits, capital gains and noncash benefits.
values.supplemental: Cash income plus qualifying noncash benefits and tax credits, less taxes, work and medical expenses, and child support paid to another household.

rows.note: Plain-language paraphrase tied to the specified original source location.

values.official: Civilian noninstitutionalized population, excluding unrelated individuals under 15 for whom poverty status cannot be determined.
values.supplemental: The official universe plus unrelated individuals under 15.

values.official: For direct comparison with SPM, the report uses official+ and assigns unrelated children under 15 the household reference person’s official poverty status.
values.supplemental: SPM includes those children; it complements the official measure and is not designed to determine programme eligibility or funding distribution.
